items.headline: Three men charged over an alleged US$18 million fake 'made in Singapore' mattress scam
items.summary: Three Singaporeans and three firms were charged with falsely declaring China-made mattresses as Singapore-made to dodge US anti-dumping duties, on goods worth over S$23 million between August 2022 and June 2025.

items.headline: CNA tops Singapore's online news rankings, with Mothership second
items.summary: The 2026 Reuters Institute Digital News Report ranked CNA the most-used online news source in Singapore (47% weekly), Mothership second (45%) and The Straits Times third (44%).

items.headline: Man jailed 11 weeks for filming upskirt videos of four women at VivoCity
items.summary: Pua Thiam Guan, 57, was jailed for 11 weeks after pleading guilty to four voyeurism charges for filming four women at VivoCity in February 2024.

items.headline: Yishun mother jailed four years for giving her teenage son methamphetamine
items.summary: A 52-year-old woman was sentenced to four years' jail for supplying her then-15-year-old son with methamphetamine between January and June 2025.

items.headline: India's top court reconsiders a 1908 rule excluding children of Parsi women
items.summary: The Supreme Court is hearing a challenge to a 1908 precedent under which only children of Parsi fathers are recognised as community members, as the Parsi population has fallen below 60,000.

items.headline: India records its driest June in over a century as the monsoon finally reaches Mumbai
items.summary: India received 53.1 mm of rain between June 4 and 22 against a normal 97.6 mm, a 46% deficit and its driest June in more than 100 years, before showers revived over Mumbai.

items.headline: Modi commissions three indigenous warships in a single day at Kolkata
items.summary: PM Modi commissioned INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak and INS Agray on June 21, all built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders, in the first commissioning of three surface combatants on one day.

items.headline: India beat New Zealand 2-0 to win the FIH Women's Nations Cup
items.summary: India beat hosts New Zealand 2-0 in the final through Navneet Kaur and Sunelita Toppo, finishing unbeaten to secure promotion back to the FIH Pro League.

items.headline: Update: Keir Starmer resigns as UK prime minister, triggering a Labour leadership contest
items.summary: Starmer announced on June 22 he will step down after losing his parliamentary party's confidence; nominations to replace him open July 9, with Andy Burnham the favourite. It puts Britain on course for its seventh leader in a decade.

items.headline: UK borrowing hit GBP23.3 billion in May, GBP5.6bn above forecast
items.summary: Public sector borrowing reached 23.3 billion pounds in May 2026, 5.6 billion above the OBR forecast, as central-government debt interest of 11.7 billion set a record for any May.

items.headline: Met Office issues a rare red extreme-heat warning as the UK's June record looks set to fall
items.summary: The Met Office issued a red extreme-heat warning for parts of England and Wales for June 24-25, with temperatures forecast to reach 38C and the UK June record of 35.6C expected to be broken.

items.headline: Two men jailed over arson attacks on properties linked to Keir Starmer
items.summary: At the Old Bailey, Roman Lavrynovych, 22, was jailed seven years and Stanislav Carpiuc, 27, two years over 2025 arson attacks on homes and a car linked to the prime minister.

items.headline: Update: US and Iran agree a 60-day roadmap toward a final deal in Switzerland
items.summary: Talks led by US VP JD Vance and Iranian Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf ended June 22 with a 60-day roadmap, Strait of Hormuz communication lines, steps to end fighting in Lebanon, and Iran agreeing to readmit nuclear inspectors.

items.headline: Update: De la Espriella wins Colombia's presidential runoff as Cepeda vows to contest
items.summary: Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella won the runoff 49.65% to Ivan Cepeda's 48.70% with nearly all ballots counted; Cepeda said his party will challenge results from 33,000 polling stations.

items.headline: China adds 10 US firms, including rare-earth miners, to its export-control list
items.summary: Beijing barred dual-use exports to 10 US firms including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth and restricted nearly 50 from government procurement, retaliating after the Pentagon listed about 80 Chinese companies.

items.headline: France closes 845 schools as a second heat dome pushes Europe toward 44C
items.summary: France closed 845 schools and placed 49 of 96 mainland departments on red alert as temperatures topped 40C, while Spain and Portugal neared 44C in Europe's second major heatwave in two months.

items.headline: Two teenagers arrested after a school shooting in the Philippines kills three
items.summary: Three students were killed and several others wounded at San Jose National High School in Tacloban on June 22; two suspects aged 14 and 15 were arrested, with police citing bullying as the apparent motive.

items.headline: SpaceX signs a compute deal worth up to $6.3 billion with open-source lab Reflection AI
items.summary: Reflection AI will pay $150 million a month from July 2026 through 2029 for Nvidia GB300 chips at SpaceX's Colossus 2 data centre near Memphis, a deal smaller than SpaceX's Anthropic and Google pacts.

items.headline: Groq confirms a $650 million raise and rebuilds after Nvidia's $20 billion talent deal
items.summary: AI-chip startup Groq confirmed a $650 million round led by Disruptive and Infinitum about six months after Nvidia licensed its technology and hired CEO Jonathan Ross; it now runs 13 data centres.

items.headline: Google DeepMind invests $75 million in studio A24 to build AI filmmaking tools
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced a $75 million investment in A24 in a first-of-its-kind partnership to co-develop AI filmmaking tools, with the studio retaining creative control.

items.headline: Microsoft and Chevron plan a 2.67-gigawatt gas plant to power a West Texas data centre
items.summary: Microsoft and Chevron unveiled Project Kilby in Reeves County, Texas, a roughly 2.67-gigawatt natural-gas plant under a 20-year power deal dedicated to a Microsoft data centre, with first power expected in 2028.

items.headline: Alphabet suffers its worst day in over a year as two top AI researchers defect
items.summary: Alphabet shares fell about 7% on June 22, its steepest drop in over a year, after Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer left for OpenAI and DeepMind's John Jumper joined Anthropic.

items.headline: AeroVironment sinks 11% on a restatement as Salesforce extends its losing streak
items.summary: Drone maker AeroVironment fell 11% on an earnings restatement, Salesforce slid for a 14th straight session (down nearly 44% in 2026), and Super Micro jumped about 14% on an Nvidia Vera Rubin product launch.

items.headline: Jio Platforms files for what would be India's biggest-ever IPO
items.summary: Reliance's Jio Platforms filed its draft prospectus with SEBI for a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, about 37,700 crore rupees, set to top Hyundai Motor India's record listing.

items.headline: The yen languishes near multi-decade lows despite a $72.8 billion intervention and a BOJ hike
items.summary: The yen sat around 160 per dollar even after Japan deployed over 11.7 trillion yen ($72.8 billion) and the Bank of Japan raised rates to 1%, its highest in three decades.

items.headline: Mercedes weigh team orders for Russell and Antonelli as Hamilton's title threat grows
items.summary: Toto Wolff says Mercedes will discuss how Antonelli and Russell race each other after they lost time scrapping in Barcelona; Antonelli leads on 156 points, 41 ahead of Hamilton, before the Austrian GP on June 28.

items.headline: West Indies beat Sri Lanka to move closer to the Women's T20 World Cup semis
items.summary: West Indies beat Sri Lanka by five wickets with 23 balls to spare at the Women's T20 World Cup in England, strengthening their push for a semi-final place.

items.headline: Bangladesh stun Pakistan as hosts England stay unbeaten at the Women's T20 World Cup
items.summary: Bangladesh beat Pakistan by 23 runs, a third straight defeat that damaged Pakistan's semi-final hopes, while hosts England made it three wins from three by beating Scotland by 38 runs.

items.headline: Jack Draper wins his first match under new coach Andy Murray at Eastbourne
items.summary: Britain's Jack Draper beat Marcos Giron 6-4, 7-6 (7-5) at the Eastbourne Open in his first match working with new coach Andy Murray, in the final grass-court tune-ups before Wimbledon.

items.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope arrives in Florida for final launch preparations
items.summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope reached Kennedy Space Center by barge on June 21, beginning final processing ahead of a launch targeted for no earlier than August 30 on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy.

items.headline: NASA's Lucy reveals a wobbling, peanut-shaped asteroid with signs of ancient water
items.summary: Lucy flyby data show asteroid Donaldjohanson tumbles every 10.5 days while wobbling every 26.5 days and carries clay minerals that form only with liquid water; the findings appear in Science.

items.headline: A tropical butterfly that barely ages could hold clues to longevity
items.summary: A Bristol-led study found Heliconius butterflies live around three times longer than relatives, with Heliconius hewitsoni reaching 348 days versus 14 for Dione juno, linked to their pollen-feeding habit.

items.headline: T. rex took about 40 years to reach full size, a new fossil study finds
items.summary: Analysing growth rings in 17 tyrannosaur specimens, researchers led by Holly Woodward concluded T. rex took roughly 40 years to reach its eight-ton adult size, far longer than the previous estimate of about 25.

fun_fact.headline: Sharks are older than trees
fun_fact.body: Sharks are older than trees. The earliest sharks appeared around 450 million years ago, while the first true trees took root about 390 million years ago, so sharks predate trees by roughly 60 million years.

puzzle.title: Same Hour, Not Twins
puzzle.body: A woman gives birth to two children at the same hour, day and year, to the same parents, yet they are not twins. How?
puzzle.approach: Question the hidden assumption that 'born together' means only two children.
puzzle.answer: They are two of a set of triplets (or more). 'Twins' means exactly two babies from one pregnancy; with three or more, any two share the same birth moment and parents without being twins.

word_puzzle.title: From Less to More
word_puzzle.body: Turn LESS into MORE in four steps, changing exactly one letter at each step; every rung must be a real word.
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at a time, keeping a valid English word on every rung.
